about: Numbers derived from real SPHEREx images, measured on 2026-11-07 on the author's machine. Only derived numbers are here: no pixels, no images, no FITS data. Every figure is copied from docs/VALIDATION.md, where the command that produced it is given, except sections 1-6, which are in real_results_generated.json (made by scratch/make_results.mjs from the real images).
limits: Six real runs on two fast-moving objects, one asteroid and one dwarf planet: not a statistical survey.

The blind Planet X search found Makemake once (a fair test, loosened options, one of 38 candidates, when an empty field gives 27–41); with the app's default options it found nothing. The distance fit works when told where to look.
WISE 0855 in D6 is a suggestive stack of 4 images, not a detection.
The bad-pixel fix for Barnard's Star in D2 was designed after seeing the error on the same images, so it is not an independent test.
Saturated stars keep a lower-limit flux. Fluxes are quick aperture sums, 2–10 % below catalogue magnitudes, not SPHEREx's own calibrated photometry.
Motion below about 1 pixel (6″) over the whole period looks like a still star; at least 3 survey passes about 6 months apart are needed.
Around a saturated star the detector's sensitivity is 20–30 times worse than in a clean field; a local background subtraction might fix this, and was not tried.
A single SPHEREx exposure reaches about V = 17: a Planet-Nine-like body is 3–5 magnitudes too faint for single images. The magnitude formulas and the Planet Nine parameters are from memory.
The calibration uses Gaussian fake stars with the PSF width of the FITS headers, on six field–detector pairs of 5′ cutouts; the empty-sky copies do not contain real variable stars.
